title: Tokenizer role idempotency fixes for multilingual onboarding, pinning & profile publish
creator: Asha Gupta
description:
Background: During onboarding of non-English model bundles we observed intermittent chat template mismatches after version pinning and profile publish. The root cause appears to be non-idempotent role delimiter normalization and language-specific tokenization heuristics that change token counts between the pre-publish validation pass and the runtime profile that gets published with the model pin. This leads to downstream latency/kv-cache mismatch, misaligned streaming boundaries, and occasional prompt truncation for customers using pinned bundles in production.

Impact: Medium–High (customer-facing regressions when a pinned bundle is published; affects multilingual bundles and templates that rely on explicit role markers). Affects Dedicated and Private onboarding flows where customers pin exact versions and ingest the published performance profile.

Goal: Make tokenizer normalization deterministic and idempotent across (a) the onboarding validation pass, (b) profile benchmarking/publishing, and (c) runtime serving so that token counts and chat template framing remain identical after pinning. Publish a regression test suite and telemetry to detect future regressions.

Proposed changes:
1) Add a deterministic role-delimiter normalizer that is applied as a single canonical pass in the onboarding pipeline and in the runtime preprocessor. This normalizer will: preserve user-visible delimiters, collapse multilingual whitespace consistently, and map equivalent Unicode separators to canonical ASCII markers only when model bundle declares `delimiter_policy: canonicalize`.
2) Introduce a tokenization snapshot artifact produced during the validation run: canonicalized input samples -> token offsets -> framing checksum. Bundle this snapshot with the profile published to the catalog. Runtime will verify snapshot checksum on first serve and report mismatch to telemetry instead of silently drifting.
3) Run the same tokenizer version (pin the tokenizer code path SHA) during benchmark runs used for performance profile publishing. Store tokenizer-sha in the published profile metadata.
4) Add onboarding checks: run golden chat templates (including multilingual samples) through the canonicalizer + tokenizer and ensure produced token counts match the snapshot used by the profile. Fail publish if mismatch; provide a remediation guide.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive canonicalization could alter user-facing messages; we will not change visible content unless model bundle explicitly requests canonicalization.
- Snapshot + checksum increases profile size and publishing time slightly; acceptable to avoid silent regressions.
- Pinning tokenizer SHA ties profile to tokenizer implementation; requires clear migration path for tokenizer upgrades (we will include an auto-rebenchmark pipeline).

Acceptance criteria: See acceptance_criteria field below for explicit tests and metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Onboarding pipeline produces a deterministic role-delimiter normalized output for all golden samples (no variance across repeated runs).
Published performance profile includes tokenizer_sha and tokenization_snapshot checksum string fields.
Runtime verifies snapshot checksum on first serve and logs mismatch as a high-severity metric; no silent truncations observed in canary traffic.
Regression test suite catches previously failing multilingual template cases (we add at least 12 new golden samples across 6 languages).
No customer-facing prompt truncation or stream boundary regressions are seen in canary after rollout for two weeks (SLO: zero latent truncation incidents).
plan: Week 1: Implement canonical role-delimiter normalizer module and unit tests; introduce tokenizer_sha capture in onboarding pipeline.
Week 2: Add tokenization snapshot artifact and checksum generator; wire snapshot into profile publish flow; update schema in catalog service (release runtime-1.19).
Week 3: Add runtime verification logic (first-serve checksum check) and non-blocking telemetry; run end-to-end internal canary with pinned bundle.
Week 4: Expand golden multilingual sample set, add regression tests to CI, and prepare PRD/Confluence guide for remediation and tokenizer upgrades.
Rollout: Canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% in Dedicated and Private regions with a 48-hour pause between phases to review telemetry.
